title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out through a fabricated interface. The victim believed he was viewing his own trading account, and the screen in front of him instead displayed AI-generated false investment information. The failure sits at the point where the user meets the platform, so the victim's own verification, which consisted of small trades, modest returns and early withdrawals, ran through the same channel that was deceiving him.

Catching it would have required account information from a source the scammers did not control, because every check made on the victim's own screen returned a false result. Detection came only when a larger withdrawal did not complete, the point at which the display and the account diverged. Police say victims in these cases rarely recover their funds.

The reporting does not establish how the false display was produced, and it describes the app both as fake and as a real app whose display was manipulated, so which account is accurate is not settled. It also does not establish that any funds were recovered or that anyone behind the scheme was identified.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple has lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway were contacted by a stranger who convinced Jerry to invest through a mobile trading app. The scammer built trust by allowing Jerry to make small trades, see modest returns, and withdraw funds initially. However, the app was fake, and scammers had created an AI-generated ghost site that showed false investment information on Jerry's screen.

When Jerry tried to withdraw a larger amount last week, he discovered the money was gone and called police. Gwinnett County investigators confirmed the trading app was real but the scammers had manipulated what Jerry saw. The couple is now speaking publicly to warn others about these sophisticated tactics. Police say victims in these cases rarely recover their funds. The Dunaways' children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help their parents with daily expenses as they work with authorities.
